dossier.public_summary: The dip seen by TESS changes dramatically from sector to sector, from over 1000 ppm to undetectable, and individual transits have wildly different depths, so the signal is not consistent with a planet. A marginal second dip suggests an eclipsing binary blended into the target aperture rather than a 2-Earth-radius planet.

reasons.why: Depth changes by more than a factor of 10 between sectors, including a non-detection in S67 (69±105 ppm). A planet on the target must have a constant depth; this requires a blended or variable source.
Change is not a calibration offset; even within SPOC 2-min the depth varies strongly (3σ), confirming astrophysical variation rather than aperture/product differences.
